main_text.l: [?]er præscripto quatuor mandatorum[?] prio-
ris Tabulæ, exhibere debemus, quod spe-
ctat,rem eodem plane modo se[?]e habe-
re contendunt. Ad ea vero quod attinet
quæ ciuilia & morali[?]a dici solent, quæ-
que sex posterioris Tabulæ mandatis
continentur, non negant superesse natu-
raliter lucis aliquid & cognitionis in ho-
minis intellectu, atque adeo in voluntate
nonnihil procliuitatis ad bonum, quan-
tumuis illud leue sit & multis modis im-
perfectum.
AMYRALDVS in ea sententia est vt
puter, non modo in rebus supernaturali-bus,
& quæ ad cultum diuinum pertinent,
sed etiam in ciuilibus atque moralibus,
corruptionem naturæ hominum tantam
esse tamque desperatam, vt si Deus eos si-
bi permitteret, nemo sit qui non eò ne-
quitiæ peruenit[?], vt cum perditissimis at-
que profligatissimis comparari possit.
Vnde sequitur vt id quidquid est
quod in homine vel vmbram boni habet dun-
taxat, profectum sit ex aliqua diuinæ Pro-
uidentiæ operatione. Sic in eo argumen-
to fines orthodoxæ doctrinæ aliquanto
quàm cæteri vlterius protulit, suamque
sententiam argumentis demonstrauit in

page.notes: Top centre: a small mark that may be the page number "5"; doubtful, so marked [?]. Line 1: "er" is doubtful, probably "ex" with a worn x. "mandatorum[?]" has an uncertain mark over the a. "spe-ctat,rem": the comma-like mark is uncertain. "se[?]e": the letter after "se" is worn. "morali[?]a": the letter is partly hidden by the fold. "eò ne-" and "peruenit[?]": "peruenit" is printed with a faint letter, likely "peruenit" or "peruenìat". "fines" and "suamque": the initial letters could be long s or f; read as fines and suamque. The "ȷ" top mark needs checking against the scan. No marginal notes, catchword or running head are printed.
